# Season 5 Patch Notes

by VisionGLLast Updated: September 25, 2026

### Advertisement

This website is supported by ads.

Last Epoch's full Season 5 Patch Notes are here! Rage of the Frostborn brings a new Season Mechanic called Rage of Morditas, which leads you on a bloody massacre through your Echoes in exchange for rewards. Paladin, Shaman, and Rogue receive new Skills, officially giving all Classes their full Skill List. Merchant's Guild and Circle of Fortune both receive significant updates. Finally, for a challenge, Last Epoch adds a new Pinnacle Boss: Morditas the God of Bloodshed. Check out our Key Takeaways below for the most notable highlights from Season 5.

##
Key Takeaways

- Rage of Morditas Season Mechanic - Rage of Morditas is a new random encounter that begins when you find and interact with Blood Crystals. When you interact with a Blood Crystal, a timer begins, and you must slay as many enemies as possible before time runs out. When the timer hits zero, an arena spawns around you, and you must face off against resurrected versions of every enemy you took down on the way. When the encounter ends, spend Bloodrage Charges gained during the Rage of Morditas mechanic on a selection of rewards. Or, use Rituals to affect the quantity, quality, or type of items offered.

- New Boss: Morditas - Completing Rage of Morditas encounters as you play fills a Rage meter. When this meter finally fills, it breaks open to reveal a special Rage of Morditas Echo Chain. This Echo Chain concludes with a fight against Morditas himself. Slaying Morditas rewards you with a Demigod's Ascendance Woven Echo. This Woven Echo requires 400 Corruption and unlocks the fight against Pinnacle Morditas. Pinnacle Morditas is between Aberroth and Uber Aberroth in difficulty.

- New Class Skills - Paladin, Shaman, and Bladedancer get their final Skills in Season 5. Paladin gets Radiant Lance, a new aggressive option that calls down holy light and fires it forward in a beam. Summon Tide Elemental rounds out the Shaman's Skill roster, offering a powerful new single Minion with a lot of versatility. Finally, Bladedancer gets Dreamslash, a low-cost spammable attack with high mobility and Shadow interactions.

- New Uniques - Season 5 brings 16 new Unique Items and a new 2-Item Set. A few of these new Unique items, such as Death's Dance, are ultra-rare chase items and are even rarer than the Red Ring of Atlaria.

- Item Faction Updates - Merchant's Guild players have access to an updated Bazaar UI, with combined Listing and Selling. A new Auto-Suggest pricing feature also suggests a price based on recent sales, and there is also a new option to incrementally lower prices on your listed items over time. In addition, Merchant's Guild players can now Purchase and List all item types upon joining the Item Faction. Circle of Fortune sees a complete rework to the Prophecy system. Instead of buying Prophecies, you now simply select what reward type you want, and your Prophecies fill and complete automatically over time as you gain Favor.

- Traveler's Rest and The Nexus - Season 5 brings a new waypoint for Traveler's Rest, formerly known as Echo of the World. This makes Traveler's Rest a physical location on your World Map. The Nexus is a new UI that gives an overview of where you are in Endgame. The Nexus shows timeline progression, Corruption levels, Blessings, Faction Progress, and other activities.

##
New Features

### Rage of Morditas

Rage of Morditas is the new random encounter you’ll discover while exploring Eterra. You’ll encounter this rage-fueled challenge in the Campaign and Monolith.

#### Encounter Basics

- This encounter can spawn in the Campaign as early as Chapter 2, and in Echoes in the form of a new interactable object, the Blood Crystal.
- In order to trigger the encounter, you must interact with a Blood Crystal.
- After starting the Rage of Morditas encounter, you will be followed by a non-corporeal Shade of Morditas who will urge you to seek out and kill as many enemies as possible.
- The event also starts a countdown timer, indicated on screen.
- Enemy kills during this phase will extend the duration of the timer with higher rarity enemies granting larger time extensions.
- The time limit increases for each enemy slain but can only be extended for so long. Try your hardest to defeat as many enemies as quickly as possible before the timer runs out. Blood vapor trails will appear that will point towards nearby enemies.
- As you defeat enemies and the Shade of Morditas collects souls, you’ll earn Bloodrage Charges that are indicated by the event progression meter underneath the mini map. Morditas will also grant you Bloodrage buffs, 1 of 28 powerful buffs is randomly selected for each Bloodrage Charge you have gained and will last for the duration of the entire encounter.
- Bloodrage Charges are accumulated by kills:
- 20 Kills → 1st BR charge
- 50 Kills → 2nd BR change
- 90 Kills → 3rd BR charge
- 140 kills → 4th BR charge
- 200 kills → 5th BR charge

- Above 200 kills, the timer goes down rapidly. Once the timer reaches zero, phase two will begin as Morditas creates a gauntlet surrounded by blood ice. During this phase, all slain enemies in phase one will revive and attempt to defeat you.
- If you wish to end phase two early, you can leave the combat area for 4 seconds to do this.
- After defeating all enemies in phase two, a Blood-Filled Crystal will take shape, allowing you to interact with it for rewards.

When you interact with the Blood-Filled Crystal, you’ll have the opportunity to spend your Bloodrage Charges to claim or modify your rewards. A single charge can:

- Claim an Item
- Once an item is claimed, the panel resets and 5 new items are generated.
- You may notice that these rewards have a new kind of Forging Potential! Ice Forging Potential has a chance to be preserved when used in crafting, and Blood Forging Potential raises the critical success chance when crafting. Only items rewarded by Rage of Morditas can have one of these new Forging Potentials.

- Perform a Frozen Ritual
- After highlighting an item, you may choose to perform a Frozen Ritual indicated by the frost rune. This ritual will allow you to sacrifice the selected reward slot, guaranteeing the remaining items are rerolled as the same item type. Let’s say you perform a Frozen Ritual on an amulet; the next set of items will only be amulets, with a higher chance of having similar affixes as the original item. Rare and exalted items will all have Ice Forging Potential.

- Perform a Bloody Ritual
- Similarly, conducting a Bloody Ritual will banish the selected slot while rerolling all other remaining reward slots, and also prevent items of the same item type as the sacrificed item from appearing. For example, using the Bloody Ritual on a 2-handed axe will mean that none of the newly rolled rewards will be 2-handed axes. This effect will last until you pick an item from the proposed set of rewards. Rare and exalted items will all have Blood Forging Potential.

- The number of Bloodrage Charges will not carry over to your next Rage of Morditas encounter, but your rewards will stay the same between encounters. Your rewards will only ever change or reset when you use a ritual or select a reward.
- To give you an idea of the rewards, here are the new item subtypes, exclusive to the Rage of Morditas Ritual encounter:
- Veinweave Belt: A belt that has 4 potion slots by default with 30-60 Mana while increasing Ward Decay Threshold by 70-100.

- Level Requirement: 50

- Gnarled Antler: A one-handed mace that gives 55 Melee Damage, 55-75% Melee Critical Strike Multiplier against Bleeding enemies, and 55-75% Melee Critical Strike Multiplier against Chilled enemies.
- Level Requirement: 50

- Warden Sceptre: A sceptre that gives 38 Melee Damage, 38-45 Spell Damage, and grants 4-8% less damage taken from chilled or bleeding enemies.

### New Endgame Boss: Morditas

- As you complete Rage of Morditas encounters in the Monolith of Fate, you’ll work to unlock three new Morditas related challenges, which can be tracked in the Nexus panel. Once Morditas has claimed enough souls, a set of special Echoes will be unlocked. In the final Echo, Circle of Frozen Blood, Morditas awaits you for a showdown.
- At the same time, defeating enemies will slowly increase Morditas’ Anger, which can be tracked in the Morditas Activity panel in the Nexus. Anger increases the difficulty and the amount of rewards you will receive after completing any of these three Echoes. If these encounters become too difficult, you can freely soothe Morditas in the Nexus panel and reduce his Anger to a more manageable level.
- New Pinnacle Woven Echo: Demigod’s Ascendance.

- Requires 400 Corruption.
- You will obtain a special Pinnacle Woven Echo after defeating the standard Morditas boss encounter in the Circle of Frozen Blood Echo. The God of Bloodshed will test your might as you step into the ring with Last Epoch’s newest pinnacle encounter, Demigod’s Ascendance.
- Nexus Window UI
- A new activity panel that can quickly select and view Endgame activities, Timelines, Dungeons, and Faction information. This is accessible in Traveler’s Rest and your world map.

- New Uniques & Set Items
- Added 16 new Uniques and 2 Set Items.

### New Skills

#### Radiant Lance

Radiant Lance imbues your shield with light from the heavens above, concentrating it into a beam of righteousness to strike down foes in front of you. Let the light of your faith guide the way, or use one of the damage conversions to take a darker path.

- Unlocked by spending 15 points in the Paladin passive tree.
- Requires a shield. Imbue your shield with light from above and concentrate it into a powerful beam that strikes enemies in front of you. Deals 1% more damage per 1% uncapped block chance (multiplicative with other modifiers).
- Added damage is applied at 500% effectiveness.
- Gains 4% increased damage per attunement.
- Mana cost: 24
- Cooldown: None
- Tags: Lightning, Spell, Area, Attunement
- Skill Tree Nodes:
- Awestruck: Radiant Lance has +100% chance to electrify per point and +100% chance to slow per point. Max 3 points.
- Conduit of Light: Radiant Lance deals 12% more ailment damage per point, and gains +1% electrify chance per point per 1% uncapped lightning resistance. Max 4 points.
- Anointed Flames: Ignite chance from all sources is converted to electrify chance for Radiant Lance. If Radiant Lance converts electrify to another ailment, then this will also convert ignite to that ailment.
- Piercing Light: Radiant Lance has +7% lightning penetration per point, doubled for ailments. Max 3 points.
- Sunbeam: Radiant Lance's base damage is converted to fire. Consequently, this damage now scales with increases to fire damage, but not increases to lightning damage. Electrify chance from all sources is converted to Ignite chance. Lightning resistance shred from all sources is converted to fire resistance shred. Effects within this tree which grant lightning penetration instead grant fire penetration. Max 1 point. This node has no effect if Abyssal Heresy is allocated.
- Solace: Radiant Lance has 10% increased mana efficiency per point. Max 3 points.
- Long Hands: When you directly cast Radiant Lance and hit at least one other ally, you cast Healing Hands on them, consuming mana equal to 100% of its mana cost. Max 1 point. This effect can only occur once per cast, regardless of the number of allies hit. "Other allies" does not include yourself.
- Radiant Inquisition: When you directly cast Radiant Lance and hit at least one boss or rare enemy, you cast Judgement on them, consuming mana equal to 140% of its mana cost. Max 1 point.
- Cloudburst: Radiant Lance no longer fires a beam forwards. It now unleashes a blast from the sky, hitting enemies within the targeted area. Radiant Lance deals 25% more damage. Max 1 point.
- Exterminatus: Radiant Lance now shoots a beam forwards and a blast from the sky. An enemy can be hit by both simultaneously. Radiant Lance has 10% less cast speed (multiplicative with other modifiers) and has +25 mana cost. Max 1 point. Effects in Radiant Lance's tree which require a direct cast can be triggered by both beams.
- Rahyeh's Fury: Radiant Lance has +2% critical strike chance per point. This effect is doubled with at least 100 attunement. Max 3 points.
- Sunrise Liturgy: Directly casting Radiant Lance also casts Divine Bolt with 2 additional projectiles per point. Radiant Lance has +1 mana cost per point. Max 3 points. Divine Bolts are not affected by your Radiant Lance tree, but can potentially be affected by your {Healing Hands} tree. An enemy can't be hit by more than 1 Divine Bolt from a single cast of Radiant Lance, but can be hit by both Radiant Lance and Divine Bolt.
- Dominion of the Sky: Radiant Lance has 25% increased area of effect per point. Max 4 points.
- Devotion: While directly casting Radiant Lance, you have additional endurance threshold equal to 20% of your maximum mana per point. Max 4 points.
- Cloudless Sky: Radiant Lance no longer requires a shield, but does not deal more damage based on your block chance. It now deals 1% more damage per 25 maximum mana (multiplicative with other modifiers). Max 1 point.
- Blessed Rain: You have a 20% chance per point to Smite enemies when they are hit by Radiant Lance. Radiant Lance has +1 mana cost per point. Max 3 points.
- Bestowed Radiance: Radiant Lance has 5% increased cast speed per point, and restores 50 health per point when directly cast. Max 3 points.
- Lay Bare: Radiant Lance has +35% chance to Shock per point and +100% lightning resistance shred chance per point. Max 3 points.
- Resplendent Aegis: Radiant Lance has +1 lightning spell damage per point per 300 block effectiveness. Max 3 points.
- Consecrated Storm: Shock chance from all sources is converted to electrify for Radiant Lance. Radiant Lance has +4% lightning penetration per stack of Electrify on the target, up to 10 stacks. Max 1 point. If Radiant Lance converts electrify to another ailment, then this will also convert shock to that ailment.
- Scathing Light: Bosses and rare enemies hit by Radiant Lance are inflicted with {Scathing Light}, an ailment that deals significant lightning and fire damage over time. Max 1 point. Scathing Light is unaffected by conversions.
- Holy Prism: Scathing Light deals 1% more damage (multiplicative with other modifiers) per 1% electrify and ignite chance with Radiant Lance.
- Essence of Divinity: You have a 10% chance per point to gain a {Divine Essence} when you use Radiant Lance and hit at least one enemy. This chance is doubled if Radiant Lance was directly cast.
- Eagle's Foot: Radiant Lance can consume 1 Divine Essence to cast two {Lesser Radiant Lances} alongside the initial cast. Max 1 point. Lesser Radiant Lance is affected by your Radiant Lance tree, but it has 50% less damage and area of effect (both multiplicative with other modifiers). An enemy cannot be hit by both Radiant Lance and a Lesser Radiant Lance from the same cast.
- Crescendo of Light: Radiant Lance can consume 3 Divine Essences to gain 50% more damage per point (multiplicative with other modifiers) and 50% increased area of effect per point. Max 3 points. When consuming 3 Divine Essences for this effect, you also gain the effect of Eagle's Foot.
- Afterglow: When you directly cast Radiant Lance or place a Reliquary, you are instilled with light for 2 seconds per point. While instilled with light, you cast Lesser Radiant Lance whenever you use a movement skill. Max 3 points.
- Avenging Wrath: Radiant Lance deals 10% more damage per point (multiplicative with other modifiers), but has +1 mana cost per point. Max 4 points.
- Sacred Vulture: Radiant Lance leeches 1% of the damage it deals as health to you per point. Max 3 points.
- Abyssal Heresy: Radiant Lance's base damage is converted to void. Consequently, this damage now scales with increases to void damage, but not increases to lightning damage. Electrify chance from all sources is converted to time rot chance. Lightning resistance shred from all sources is converted to void resistance shred. Effects within this tree which grant lightning penetration instead grant void penetration. Radiant Lance no longer scales with attunement, and instead gains spell void damage per vitality. Max 1 point. Effects in Radiant Lance's tree which grant or consume Divine Essences will instead grant or consume Void Essences.
- Golden Reliquary: You no longer directly cast Radiant Lance. Instead, you place a Reliquary that casts it for you for 6 seconds. Reliquaries have 55% less cast speed, resulting in a base cast rate of once every 2 seconds. You can have a maximum of 1 Reliquary by default, and gain +1 max Reliquaries per 70 attunement. Reliquaries casting Radiant Lance count as you indirectly casting it. This means it still scales with your stats, not the minion's stats. For example, to increase how frequently they cast Radiant Lance, you must increase your cast speed. Max 1 point.
- Righteous Preservation: Reliquaries have 20% more health per point (multiplicative with other modifiers). Max 2 points.

#### Summon Tide Elemental

Shamans can summon the new Tide Elemental to fight by their side, a permanent manifestation of the icy depths of Eterra’s oceans. Command it to wield powerful Cold spells or choose from several damage conversions to unleash nature’s wrath.

- Unlock by spending 30 points in the Shaman passive tree.
- Summon a manifestation of the elements to fight alongside you. The tide elemental is a permanent minion that uses cold spells. If your minions are set to Assassinate mode, your tide elemental will teleport to its target when casting Geyser.
- You can have a maximum of 1 elemental at a time. It uses a projectile spell with no cooldown, and can create a powerful Geyser spell that deals damage in an area, with a 4 second cooldown. It also casts Geyser when summoned. Elementals have 400 base health.
- Gains +16 health and 4% increased damage per attunement, and +16 health per character level.
- Added minion spell damage applies to its projectiles at 200% effectiveness and to its Geyser at 400% effectiveness.
- Mana cost: 15
- Cooldown: 4s
- Minion Tags: Cold, Spell, Area
- Skill Tree Nodes:
- King Tide: 8% more damage per point. Max 4 points.
- High Tide: 3% more damage per second your tide elemental has been alive per point, up to 6 seconds. Max 3 points.
- Crashing Waves: +2% critical strike chance per point, +12% critical strike multiplier per point. Max 3 points.
- Mana Swell: +1% critical strike chance per 100 maximum mana per point. Max 2 points.
- Tidal Pools: Geyser has a 10% chance per point to repeat from each totem within 12 meters. Each cast can hit the same enemy. Repeated casts can't trigger additional repeats. Max 3 points.
- Azure Expanse: Geyser has 30% increased area per point. Max 3 points.
- Ocean Currents: Geyser has 34% increased cooldown recovery speed per point. Max 3 points.
- Resurgence: Summon Tide Elemental no longer has a cooldown, but costs +5 mana. The Geyser that occurs when casting Summon Tide Elemental deals 40% more damage and has 25% increased area.
- Artesian Well: While you are above half mana, Geyser consumes your mana to also cast Elemental Bolt once per point, targeting enemies within 12 meters. Consumes 8 mana per cast of Elemental Bolt.
- Water Spout: When one of your Tornadoes hits your tide elemental, the tide elemental redirects it towards an enemy within 12 meters and grants the Tornado 20% more damage and speed per point for 3 seconds. A Tornado can only be redirected once, and stationary Tornadoes can't be redirected. Max 3 points.
- Twin Twisters: Whenever you create a Tornado at least 4 meters away from your tide elemental, you have a 12% chance per point to create a Tornado at your tide elemental's location as well. This Tornado is instantly redirected by Water Spout. Max 3 points.
- Crimson Harbor: Your tide elemental gains 100% of your mana regeneration as increased health regeneration per point. It also gains +10 health regeneration per point. Max 4 points.
- Return to Seafoam: If your tide elemental dies, its cooldown is reset. Your Tide Elemental has 20% more health. Max 1 point.
- Wellspring: Your tide elemental gains Wellspring, an aura that grants +4 cold spell damage per point and 2% increased cast speed per point to allies within 18 meters. Max 4 points. Wellspring affects all allies, including itself. If your tide elemental's damage is converted, the additional spell damage from wellspring is also converted. If there are multiple tide elementals, only the strongest Wellspring applies.
- Pools of Reverence: Wellspring's buffs are 100% more effective on totems, but it no longer affects players. Max 1 point.
- Harmony of Water: Wellspring's buffs have 0.5% increased effect on players per point per your attunement. Max 4 points.
- Bird Bath: Wellspring grants storm crows a 25% chance per point for their basic lightning spell to chain to two additional enemies. Max 3 points.
- Whirlpools: Your tide elemental has a 25% chance per point to cast Maelstrom whenever you do. Maelstroms cast by your tide elemental in this way use your tide elemental's stats, but your Maelstrom tree. Max 4 points.
- Cove of Gulls: Your tide elemental deals 6% more damage per point per active storm crow. Max 2 points.
- Erosion: Your tide elemental has a 25% chance per point to shred cold resistance on hit. Max 4 points.
- Seahenge: When you summon your tide elemental, your totems are moved to surround it. Each totem moved this way gains +2 seconds of duration, up to a maximum of 6. Max 1 point.
- Northern Seas: Your tide elemental has a 25% chance to inflict frostbite on hit per point. This effect is doubled with at least 80 attunement. Max 4 points.
- Tidal Totem: Your tide elemental is now a totem. It cannot move, but is affected by totem modifiers. Your tide elemental deals 20% more damage. Max 1 point.
- Riptide: Your tide elemental has 8% increased cast speed and movement speed per point. Max 4 points.
- Thunder Elemental: Your tide elemental becomes a thunder elemental. The base cold damage of your elemental's spells are converted to lightning. Consequently, this damage scales with increases to lightning damage, but not with increases to cold damage. Frostbite chance and cold resistance shred from all sources are converted to shock chance and lightning resistance shred, respectively. Your elemental gains +20% critical strike multiplier. Max 1 point.
- Wind Elemental: Your tide elemental becomes a Wind Elemental. The base cold damage of your elemental's spells are converted to physical. Consequently, this damage scales with increases to physical damage, but not with increases to cold damage. Frostbite chance and cold resistance shred from all sources are converted to frailty chance and physical resistance shred, respectively. Your elemental gains +200 dodge rating. Max 1 point.
- Wake: Your tide elemental's Elemental Bolt fires 1 additional projectile in a cone per point. Max 2 points. Elemental Bolt's projectiles cannot hit the same target more than once per cast.
- Backflow: Elemental Bolt's projectiles are fired in a nova, targeting enemies within 12 meters. Elemental Bolt fires 3 additional projectiles, but your Tide Elemental has 10% less cast speed. Max 1 point.
- Elemental Fury: When your tide elemental directly casts Elemental Bolt it gains Elemental Fury for 4 seconds, stacking up to a maximum of 5. Each stack of Elemental Fury grants 5% increased cast speed for Elemental Bolt. Max 1 point.
- Unleashed Elements: When your tide elemental directly cast Elemental Bolt while at maximum stacks of Elemental Fury, it consumes all stacks to gain an additional projectile per stack. Elemental Bolt cast this way fires its projectiles in a tight volley, and can hit the same target multiple times. Max 1 point.

#### Dreamslash

Close the gap and strike your enemies with a quick slash attack that can be combined with your Shadows, increasing your damage output even further. With a high attack speed build, you’ll be zipping around the battlefield, leaving a wake of destruction.

- Unlock by spending 10 points in the Bladedancer passive tree.
- Requires a melee weapon. Dash forwards if not within range of your target, hitting all enemies along the path, then perform a quick slash. Shadows performing Dreamslash dash beyond their target, hitting all enemies along the path.
- Added damage applies at 150% effectiveness. Shadows will only be consumed if within 12 meters of the target. The dash and slash deal the same amount of damage, and an enemy can only be hit by one of them.
- Gains 4% increased damage per dexterity.
- Mana cost: 3
- Cooldown: None
- Tags: Physical, Melee, Area, Movement, Dexterity
- Skill Tree Nodes:
- Umbral Recollection: Shadows performing Dreamslash have +10% chance per point to be resummoned after completing the attack. Max 3 points. Resummoning a shadow means the shadow is consumed and a new shadow is created at its position.
- Veil of Night: Dreamslash has +34% chance per point to blind enemies, and deals more 8% damage per point to blinded enemies (multiplicative with other modifiers). Max 3 points.
- Collapsing Shadows: Dreamslash has +25% chance per point to inflict Shadow Daggers on hit. This is doubled for shadows performing Dreamslash.
- Deadly Premonitions: Dreamslash has +3% critical strike chance per point. Max 3 points.
- Distortion Blade: Dreamslash has 5% increased attack speed per point, and -1 mana cost per point. Max 3 points.
- Illusory Edge: Dreamslash deals 8% more damage per point (multiplicative with other modifiers). Max 4 points.
- Imaginary Plate: Dreamslash hits have +35% chance per point to shred enemy armor. Max 3 points.
- Figments of Annihilation: Dreamslash has +5% critical strike multiplier per point per shadow performing Dreamslash. Max 3 points. This applies to your use of Dreamslash and to all shadows performing Dreamslash, based on the number of shadows that will be performing Dreamslash from this use.
- Grand Delusion: Dreamslash has 20% increased area of effect per point. This is doubled when using a two-handed weapon. Max 3 points.
- Domain of Night: Shadows performing Dreamslash have 25% increased area of effect per point. Max 3 points.
- Wounds in Reality: Dreamslash has +15% chance per point to cause enemies to bleed. When you directly use Dreamslash and hit an enemy, you have a 1% chance per point per bleed on that enemy to create a shadow nearby the enemy. This effect has a 1 second cooldown. Max 3 points.
- Sleep Paralysis: Dreamslash has +25% chance per point to inflict frostbite and +12% chance per point to inflict chill on hit. Max 4 points.
- Somnambulism: Shadows performing Dreamslash also use a random specialized throwing skill, consuming mana equal to 100% of that skill's mana cost. This effect can occur 3 times per point per 3 seconds, and will not choose skills that have a cooldown. Max 3 points. This does not cause you to create or consume additional shadows. Effects in this tree related to shadows performing Dreamslash do not apply to these throwing skills.
- Gathering Darkness: Dreamslash deals 2% more damage per point (multiplicative with other modifiers) per shadow created in the past 3 seconds, up to a maximum of 20% per point. Dreamslash now has a minimum mana cost of 1. Max 3 points.
- Recurring Dreams: Up to 1 shadow per point performing Dreamslash can consume 5 mana to guarantee being resummoned. Max 4 points. If a shadow is successfully resummoned by other sources such as Umbral Recollection, it will be ignored by this effect.
- Prophecy of Flames: Dreamslash has +25% chance per point to ignite enemies. This is doubled for shadows performing Dreamslash. Max 4 points.
- Shrouded Dreams: Dreamslash has +20% chance per point to cause enemies to bleed per Crimson Shroud, +5% chance per point to slow enemies per Dusk Shroud, and grants +10 ward on hit per point per Silver Shroud. Max 3 points.
- Gift of Lucidity: Dreamslash has +10% chance on hit per point to grant Haste for 1 second. Dreamslash has 4% increased attack speed per point while you have Haste. Max 3 points. Increased attack speed while you have Haste is affected by increased effect of Haste on you.
- Narcolepsy: You gain a stack of Dream every 2 seconds, up to a maximum. Directly using Dreamslash can consume a Dream stack to grant the attack 120% more damage (multiplicative with other modifiers) and cause it to choose a random nearby target.
- Shared Memories: When you directly use Dreamslash and consume a Dream stack, Dreamslash has a 15% chance per point to refract towards an enemy within 8 meters. This can hit the same enemies again. The refraction will occur even if there are no other enemies for it to refract towards.
- Inception: Refracted Dreamslashes can also refract, but the chance to refract is halved after each refraction. Max 1 point.
- Night Terror: You have +5% chance per point to gain a Dream stack when you kill an enemy or hit a boss or rare enemy with Dreamslash, and Dreamslash has +3% critical strike chance per point when consuming a Dream stack. Max 3 points.
- Dreamwalker: 1% increased Dream gain rate per point per 3 dexterity. Max 3 points. For example with 3 points invested and 100 dexterity, you have 100% increased {Dream} gain rate, resulting in gaining one stack every 1 second instead of every two seconds.
- Dreamshift: Shadows no longer perform Dreamslash. If you directly use Dreamslash while you have no Dream stacks, you will consume a shadow near an enemy to gain a Dream stack and perform Dreamslash starting from the shadow's location. Max 1 point. The use of Dreamslash which consumes a shadow does not consume the Dream stack it generates, but still benefits as if it consumed a Dream stack. Shadows are not chosen to be consumed if they are not within range of an enemy.
- Trance of Isolation: Dreamslash's base physical damage is converted to cold. Consequently this damage scales with increases to cold, but not to physical damage.  Bleed chance and ignite chance from all sources are converted to frostbite chance. Max 1 point. This node has no effect if Apocalyptic Vision is allocated.
- Apocalyptic Vision: Dreamslash's base physical damage is converted to fire. Consequently this damage scales with increases to fire, but not to physical damage.  Bleed chance and frostbite chance from all sources are converted to ignite chance. Chill chance from all sources is converted to fire resistance shred chance. Max 1 point.
- Nightmare Steel: Dreamslash no longer moves you. It instead unleashes a wave of damage in the targeted direction, hitting all enemies in its path. It is still a melee attack. Max 1 point.

- Trance of Wrath: When you use Dreamslash you gain Dream Aura for 4 seconds, which has a radius equal to Dreamslash's range. While Dream Aura is active, enemies within its range have +5% chance to receive critical strikes. While you do not have Dream Aura active, Dreamslash has 20% increased range.

### Faction Changes

#### Merchant's Guild

- Added Price Suggestion
- When listing an item for sale, a price suggestion will be provided based on item price history data.
- NOTE: At the very beginning of a Season, items won’t have a price history yet. You can hold onto the item until there is more pricing data, or take the initiative and help define that item’s value!

- Reworked Rank and Rank Rewards
- All equippable item types can now be purchased simply by being a member of the Merchant’s Guild, regardless of rank.
- Ranks now unlock access to purchase various bags that contain crafting materials or keys.
- Removed Black Market tokens.

- Added opt-in Automatic Price Lowering.
- When listing an item, you can now choose to have it's price automatically lower over time, so you can spend less time relisting items and more time slaying monsters.
- When enabling price lowering, you can select:
- A price floor that the Bazaar will never reduce your item's price below.
- A lowering amount either as a flat value or a percent of your original list price.
- A lowering frequency of hourly, daily, or weekly.

- When shopping for items, the stall type can now be swapped from the interface without walking to another NPC.
- Reworked the Bazaar user interface for a more streamlined experience.
- The list item panel has been removed, and items are now listed directly from the sidebar so you can view search results and list an item from the same UI.
- Placing an item to sell will automatically apply quick filtering (previously only on Shift + Right-click).
- Placing an item will now also provide a suggested price.
- Price suggestions are based on recent market sales of similar items.
- Additional price suggestions and a breakdown of what attributes of the item contributed to it’s market price are available in an info tooltip next to the suggested price.

- Filters have been reorganized to put the most commonly used filters at the top and group similar filters together.
- Some filters are now only shown when another relevant filter has a value.
- Legendary Potential only shows if a Unique is selected that can roll Legendary Potential.
- Weaver’s Will only shows if a unique is selected that can roll Weaver’s Will.
- Forging Potential only shows if the rarity is set to Normal, Magic, Rare, or Exalted.

- Added new affix filtering options.
- Added # of T6 affixes filter.
- Both # of T6 and # of T7 affixes filters now ignore sealed affixes to make finding Havoc/Redemption targets easier.
- Added more groups to the affix picker to allow for more specific searches.
- All (renamed from Require All).
- Any (renamed from Require Any).
- Prefixes (only matches non-sealed prefixes).
- Suffixes (only matches non-sealed suffixes).
- Non-Sealed (only matches non-sealed affixes).
- Sealed (only matches sealed affixes).

- Any, Prefixes, Suffixes, Non-Sealed, and Sealed affix groups also include an optional min count for controlling how many of the selected affixes in that group must match. For example, you can now search for at least 1 of 5 selected prefixes, 2 of 4 selected suffixes, and 1 of 10 selected sealed in a single query.

#### Circle of Fortune

- Removed Prophecy rerolling.
- You now select the reward category you want for a prophecy slot, and it will gain charges (up to 99) as you gain Favor with the Circle of Fortune.
- Completing one of a prophecy's designated targets while it has a charge will grant you the selected rewards.
- Reworked the prophecy system with the goals of:
- Reduce time spent in the Observatory so you can get back to slaying monsters faster.
- Provide more agency in directly choosing your rewards.
- Reduce specificity of targets so prophecies can be fulfilled across a variety of content.

- There are now 4 prophecy slots. Your first slot is unlocked as you join Circle of Fortune, with the rest unlocking as you rank up.

### Prophecies

- Each prophecy slot has two trigger conditions, and fulfilling either one qualifies you to earn rewards from a charge.
- For example, the Dysis prophecy slot (unlocked at rank 3) targets defeating a Nemesis or opening a Lost Cache.

- Completing a trigger condition while its prophecy slot has at least one charge grants the selected reward at the cost of a single charge.
- If a prophecy slot has multiple charges when its trigger condition is fulfilled, multiple charges will be spent, dropping the rewards multiple times.
- The 4 prophecy slots are:
- Mesembria:
- Unlocked at rank 1.
- Defeat a Rift Beast or activate a Shrine.

- Dysis:
- Unlocked at rank 3.
- Defeat a Nemesis or open a Lost Cache.

- Eos:
- Unlocked at rank 6.
- Defeat an Exiled Mage or Timeline Boss.

- Arctis:
- Unlocked at rank 9.
- Defeat a Fateweaver or an Omen.

### Reward Selection

- When using a telescope to select your prophecy, you now directly select the type of reward you want.
- Once a reward is chosen, the prophecy slot will automatically charge up as you gain favor.
- Each reward type has been tuned so you get similar numbers of items per favor as before.
- You can see how much favor it will take to earn a charge in the tooltip for each reward type.
- As you rank up, you will unlock more rewards as options to pick from in your prophecy slots.
- Some rewards upgrade at higher ranks, such as rare item rewards being replaced by exalted items of the same type.
- When a selected reward upgrades it will happen automatically with no need for a trip back to the Observatory.

- As you rank up, you will also unlock the ability to purchase lenses at the faction vendor.
- Lenses only need to be purchased once and will be available to all characters with access to the same stash.
- Lenses automatically move to storage when purchased, so you don't need to devote any stash tab space to them.

- You can slot 1 reward and 1 lens into each prophecy slot.
- Each reward and lens can only be used in 1 prophecy slot per character, but multiple characters can use the same reward or lens.
- Whenever you earn favor, all prophecy slots will gain charge progress based on the reward and lens selected.
- When a prophecy fully charges, it will store 1 charge and can hold up to 99 total.
- If a prophecy has at least 1 charge, completing it's target objective will consume a charge to drop the chosen reward.
- If a prophecy has multiple charges, it will consume extra charges to drop the reward additional times.

- The selection types of prophecy rewards increase each rank. They are as follows:
- Rank 1:
- Rare (each equipment item type).
- Unique (each equipment item type).
- Set Weapon or Offhand, Jewelry, Armor.
- Random Idol.
- Rune of Shattering, Rune of Discovery.
- Glyph of Hope, Glyph of Chaos.

- Rank 2:
- Rune of Removal.
- Glyph of Order.
- Random Key.

- Rank 3:
- Rune of Shaping, Rune of Refinement.
- Temporal Sanctum Key, Lightless Arbor Key, Soulfire Bastion Key.

- Rank 4:
- All Rare gear rewards upgrade to Exalted.
- Small, Minor, Humble, Stout, Grand, Large, Ornate, Huge, Adorned Idol.
- Unique Idol.
- Random Rune.
- Random Glyph.

- Rank 5:
- Rare Idol Altar.
- Arena Key, Arena Key of Memory.
- Dungeon Charms.
- Rare Champion Item.

- Rank 6:
- Rare Harbinger's Spoils (weapon/off hands that upgrade when slaying a Harbinger).
- Rare Experimental Item.

- Rank 7:
- Rare Champion Item upgrades to Exalted.

- Rank 8:
- Small, Minor, Humble, Stout Weaver Idol.
- Rune of Weaving.
- Rare Experimental Item upgrades to Exalted.

- Rank 9:
- Exalted Champion Item upgrades to T6+ (champion affix is always T6 or higher).

- Rank 10:
- Rare Idol Altar upgrades to Exalted.
- Rare Harbinger's Spoils upgrades to Exalted.
- Exalted Experimental Item upgrades to T6+ (experimental affix is always T6 or higher).
- Glyph of Despair, Glyph of Envy.

- Rank 11:
- Rune of Redemption, Rune of Havoc, Rune of Ascendance, Rune of Creation.
- T6+ Exalted Champion Item upgrades to T7 (champion affix is always T7).

- Rank 12:
- T6+ Exalted Experimental Item upgrades to T7 (experimental affix is always T7).

### Lenses

- Added Lenses, which are used to alter the characteristics of prophecies and can be purchased from Galila.
- Lenses are unlocked for your entire stash once purchased.
- Lenses can affect charge rate, items dropped, or aspects of the rewards, such as affixes or Legendary Potential.
- Rank 3:
- Tyranny consumes existing favor to double the charge rate.

- Rank 4:
- Origin causes rare and exalted rewards to have higher tiers of prefixes on average.
- Finality causes rare and exalted rewards to have higher tier suffixes on average.

- Rank 5:
- Celerity causes the prophecy to charge faster.
- Duplication grants a chance to duplicate prophecy rewards.

- Rank 6:
- Acceleration adds Rare Enemies as a target condition.
- Anomaly causes rare and exalted rewards to have compressed affix weighting (e.g. level of skills is more common and strength is less common).
- Prowess causes Helmet, Body Armor, and Relic rewards to have a higher chance for level of skills affixes.

- Rank 7:
- Charity causes other prophecy slots to charge faster.
- Celestial Scales grants a chance to double rewards, but also a small chance to replace all rewards with a single reassuring Grole Egg.

- Rank 8:
- Curiosity causes Unique and Set Items to have compressed weighting (e.g. Red Ring is more common and Kestral is less common).

- Rank 9:
- Quality causes unique rewards to have higher average Legendary Potential and grants rare or exalted rewards a chance to upgrade the tier of a random affix.

### Traveler's Rest

- Echo of the World has been renamed to Traveler’s Rest.
- Traveler’s Rest now has a waypoint, which can be accessed from the End of Time Era.
- You can now change timelines directly from the Monolith of Fate through the new Nexus UI.

##
Content Updates

### Free Cosmetic: Cape of Penance

- Added a free back cosmetic to the in-game store redeemable by all players for free.

### Campaign - Quest Reward Changes

- The quests for defeating Majasa and The Observer no longer award +1 to all attributes.
- The quest for gathering 5 Knowledge of Orobyss now gives +2 to all attributes.
- The quests for defeating The Observer now gives +1 passive point.

### Monolith

- Entering an echo that has previously been attempted now provides significantly less XP and favor, in addition to the existing reductions to random encounters and loot.
- This is to prevent a burden of optimal play being to spam run the same echo over and over (looking at you, Rune Prison Complex).

### Random Encounters

- Added three new one shot caches with dungeon keys in out of the way locations. Once found, these offer a single chance to use each dungeon to bypass part of the campaign on your first character of a season or a solo character.
- Loot lizards spawn less frequently in campaign.

### Omen Windows

- Omen Windows can start appearing as early as area level 18 (from 10).
- Omen Windows can start dropping Idol Altars as early as area level 32 (from 10).
- Idol Altars have a 40% chance to drop from area level 32-49 (from 100%).
- Idol Altars have a 80% chance to drop from area level 50-79 (from 100%).
- Idol Altars dropped in area levels 50-79 will drop with 1-2 affixes (from always 2).
- Omen Windows are now only announce by proximity instead of at scene entry.

##
Class & Skill Updates

### General Skill Changes

- Attempting to use an instant cast ability while stunned will now result in that ability being used when the stun ends rather than nothing happening.
- When an ailment’s duration resets, it also resets its remaining total damage to its original value when it was applied, allowing the ailment to deal its full damage again.

#### Evade

- Evade movement now takes the full duration to stop, even when used near movement area edges or obstacles.

### Rogue

#### Aerial Assault

- Twilight Strike now throws half as many blades if Umbral Blades throws large blades due to Sword Thrower.

#### Dancing Strikes

- Corrected the description of Resolute Technique to state it grants more damage for Lethal Mirage and Synchronized Strikes (previously erroneously said increased damage). This is only a display change.

#### Dark Quiver

- Black arrow drops from Dark Quiver are now biased towards the direction the player is facing.

#### Flurry

- Reduced the range of Flurry with a bow.

#### Hail of Arrows

- Crystal Arrows also converts bleed chance from all sources to frostbite.
- Frost Shots no longer grants increased 20% chill duration per point. It now grants +50% frostbite chance per second per point. Max 4 points (from 5).
- Tear Flesh grants +50% bleed chance per second per point (from 40%). Max 4 points (from 5).
- Skystrike no longer grants 25% increased mana cost.
- Quick Draw grants 8% less duration per point (from 10%).
- Backup Volley grants 20% less duration (from 50%).
- Deadly Draw grants 15% increased delay (from 25%).
- Endless Barrage now also grants 50% more damage, and its description has been corrected to state the mana cost per second is 15 (previously incorrectly said 23).

#### Lethal Mirage

- Doom and Gloom now has a 5% chance per point to create a Shadow when a Mirage hits an enemy (previously 5% chance per Mirage created).
- Added a new Skill Tree Node named Prestige that provides an escape dash to the end of the Lethal Mirage damage window. If movement and invulnerability are disabled on Lethal Mirage, instead provides a short dash with no wait period.

#### Puncture

- Penumbral Ambush grants +12 mana cost (from +15), and it now also grants 30% more hit damage. Its description has been updated to clarify it can potentially hit the same enemy multiple times.
- Perforate grants +25% bleed chance per point (from 20%). Max 4 points (from 5).
- Toxic Delivery grants +25% poison chance per point (from 20%).
- Cadence of Death grants 30% more damage and increased area for the third hit (from 20%).
- Splinter grants +25% physical resistance shred chance per point (from 20%). Max 4 points (from 5).
- Seized Prey grants 4% more damage per point against slowed enemies (from 4% more hit damage) and 8% more damage against immobilized enemies (from 8% more hit damage).
- Inescapable grants 5% more damage per point per slow on the target (from 5% more hit damage).
- Debilitation grants 1.5% more damage per point per unique negative ailment on the target up to 8 (from 7% more hit damage per unique negative ailment on the target, up to 1 per point)

- Updated Onslaught's description to clarify that it only grants mana when Shadow Cascade is directly used.

- The Entry Points node now determines its damage based on the combined total of Bleed and Poison stacks, rather than counting each ailment separately.

- Moonlight Bomb now adds a minimum cooldown of 6 seconds to Smoke Cloud.
- Cloaked Incursion now limits you to 1 Smoke Cloud active at once.

#### Summon Ballista

- Placement range limit is now 4 (from 20).

#### Synchronized Strike

- Synchronized Strike is now locked to Bladedancer, acquired at 35 points invested (from 10).

#### Umbral Blades

- Subzero Intrusion now also converts bleed chance from all sources to frostbite.
- Edge of Obscurity grants 1% more damage per point (from 2%) per stack of Dusk Shroud on you up to 20, and is no longer doubled while in a Smoke Cloud.
- Umbral Remnant's "whenever one of your shadows expire they now also leave behind an Umbral Blade" now has a limit of 12 times per 2 seconds (from no limit).
- Thousand Cuts now has a maximum of +40% critical strike multiplier gained from this effect per point (from no limit).

#### Marksman Passive Tree

- Fire and Steel has been replaced with Careful Footing: +1 dexterity per point, +1% glancing blow chance per point, and 1% increased movement speed per point. Max 8 points. It also has a 6-point threshold bonus which grants +1% glancing blow chance per 5 dexterity.
- Siege Quiver has been replaced with Ranger: 1% increased health per point and +3% elemental resistance per point. Max 5 points. No longer requires any points in Elemental Arrows.

- Poison Tipped Arrows grants +3% poison penetration per point (from 2%).
- Barbed Arrows grants +10% bleed chance per point (from 5%) and 7% increased physical damage per point (from 5%).
- Death From Afar no longer grants 4% increased stun chance per stack of Sharpshooter per point. It now grants +0.2% chance to deal double damage per stack of Sharpshooter per point.

### Acolyte

#### Bone Curse

- Self-inflicted Bone Curse no longer scales with player stats, similar to other self-inflicted curses. This means that your damage modifiers won't increase the damage it deals to you.

#### Profane Veil

- Propane Form no longer reduces Profane Veil's duration.

#### Rip Blood

- Updated the description of Coagulated Blood's buff icon to correctly state that orbs are spawned on reaching 6 stacks instead of 4.
- Coagulation will now attempt to consume as many stacks of Coagulated Blood as possible, still in groups of 6, to cast 1 Coagulated Blood Orb per 6 stacks consumed. For example, with 12 stacks, one cast of Rip Blood will now consume 12 stacks to create 2 orbs.

#### Summon Bone Golem

- Cooldown is now 3 seconds (from 10), and mana cost is 30 (from 35).
- Twin Golems has had its description clarified to state it summons an additional golem when directly cast.

#### Summon Skeleton

- Individual Operator's benefit for Skeleton Rogues now caps out at a combined total of 5 Skeleton Warriors or Archers (from no cap).
- Empty the Graves has had its description clarified to state it summons additional skeletons when directly cast.

#### Wandering Spirits

- Updated the description of the Haunting node so that it no longer incorrectly states that the node would reduce the area of the Fear.

#### Acolyte Passive Tree

- The Revenant from the Ethereal Revenant node has had its Whirling Scythes ability changed to a melee attack (was previously a throwing attack). This is only a change to its tags, its functionality is unchanged.

### Sentinel

#### Anomaly

- Explosive Lash requires Flame Alchemist instead of Explosive Impact.

- Soot and Ash grants +20% blind chance per point and +20% frailty chance per point (previously the benefits were exclusive to bow and melee respectively).
- Pocket Sand's effect has been replaced: +2% critical strike chance per point and 5% more damage to blinded enemies per point (previously converted blind chance to critical vulnerability chance). Max 3 points.
- Ignition grants +25% ignite chance per point (from 20%) and 12% increased ignite duration for the first strike per point (from 10%). Max 4 points (from 5).

- Coated Darts grants +2 throwing fire damage per point for each stack of Oil Coating (from +1). Max 3 points (from 5).
- Elusive grants +15 dodge rating per point and +4% fire resistance per point for each stack of Oil Coating (from +10 and +3%). Max 4 points (from 5).
- Oil Coating grants 8% increased fire damage per point for each stack of Oil Coating (from 5%). Max 4 points (from 5).
- Blast Wave grants 15% more first attack damage per point (from 10%).

#### Forge Strike

- Ricochet's description has been updated to state more clearly that Hammer Throw no longer throws extra projectiles.

- Urgent Inquisition grants 75% less healing (from 50%), and now also grants 25% less damage for Consecrated Ground.

#### Ring of Shields

- Amass now requires 1 point in Bastion (from 3).
- Rush Wall now also causes the cast of Shield Rush to gain 30% more damage per contributing shield, but the shields are destroyed when Shield Rush ends. Requires 1 point in Defensive Shields (from 2).
- Healing Shields heals every 4 seconds (from every 6).

This chance is instead 5% if Shield Throw has a cooldown. Max 1 point. This effect will not occur if there are no enemies within 12 meters.
- Touched by Fire has been replaced with Combined Might: Each shield grants you +1 physical damage per point for attacks and spells. Max 3 points, and now requires Enduring Defense instead of Molten Shields. This effect's benefit can be converted to fire by Molten Shields.

Max 2 points. This only affects buffs which are granted exclusively to you, not to any allies.

#### Avalanche

- Mountain's Fury grants 20% increased impact area per point (from 15%). Max 3 points (from 4).
- Unyielding Storm causes Avalanche to persist after channeling for twice the duration you spent channeling (from 1x the duration), up to a maximum of 3 seconds per point (from 1.5 seconds).

- Toxic Envelopment grants +100% poison chance (from +40%) per point and now also grants 6% more damage per point. Max 4 points (from 5).

- Added a new node connected to Shredding Vines, Destructive Growth: Root Wave lowers the physical resistance of affected enemies by 8% per point for the duration of the root. Max 3 points.
- Blooming Magic grants other allies +10 spell damage (from +8) per point. Max 4 points (from 5)
- Bush Stalkers grants your wolves and bear +5% crit chance (from +4%) per point and +15% critical multiplier (from +10%) per point. Max 4 points (from 5).
- Added a new node connected to Nourishment Surge, Flourish: 15% increased mana efficiency per point. Max 3 points.
- Nourishment Surge now also grants 12% increased area per point.
- Lethal Spines grants 6% more damage over time per second (from 5%) per point. Max 4 points (from 5).

#### Gathering Storm

- Storm Bolts now prioritize enemies over destructible objects. Those barrels probably deserved it, though.

#### Serpent Strike

- Corrosive Venom no longer says it grants a chance to shred poison resistance. This is only a description change.

- Winged Raptor now gives the Storm Crow 50% more health (from 30%), 50% more damage (from 30%), 50% increased size (from 30%), and grants it the ability to use Storm Surge, a skill that causes the crow to dash through enemies and cast its basic lightning spell 4 times.

#### Swarmblade Form

- Locust Master has been replaced with Stormslash: When you use Armblade Slash and hit at least one enemy, you consume 1 rage to gain a Storm Stack. Max 1 point.
- Spiked Vespiary is no longer limited to casting Thorns as many times as it would summon locusts.
- Death by a Thousand Wings grants +30% bleed chance per point for Armblade Slash (from 20%), +150% bleed chance per point for Dive (from 100%), and +30% bleed chance per point for Locusts (from 20%). Max 3 points (from 5).
- Wasp Flight grants 6% increased attack and cast speed per point (from 5%). Max 4 points (from 5).
- Earth Stinger grants +4 melee physical damage per point for you and your locusts (from 3). Max 4 points (from 5).
- Needle-Like Sting grants +3% critical strike chance per point for you and your locusts (from 2%). Max 4 points (from 5).
- Feverous Stings grants +30% poison chance per point for you and your locusts (from 20%). Max 4 points (from 5).
- Grand Colony grants +2 max locusts summoned per point (from 1) and +2 locusts summoned from each hive per point (from 1).
- Locust Agility grants +60 armor and dodge rating per point for you and your locusts (from 40). Max 4 points (from 5).
- Slashing Spiral grants 25% increased area per point for Swarm Strike, Locust Swarm, and your locusts' melee attacks (from 20%). Max 4 points (from 5).
- Vampiric Mandibles now also grants 8% more Locust Swarm damage per point.

#### Tempest Strike

- Mana cost is now 12 (from 16).
- The melee attacks now have a damage effectiveness of 200% (from 100%).
- The damage effectiveness of the spell subskills has been changed: Frigid Tempest has 300% (from 150%), Wind Tempest has 200% per second (from 150% per second), and Thunder Tempest has 200% (from 100%), with an equivalent base damage for each.
- Attuned Slam grants 1.5% more damage per point per mana cost (from 1%).
- Ancestral Swiftness has a maximum of 3 points (from 2).
- Soaring Blows requires 1 point in Ancestral Swiftness (from 2).
- Calm Seas, Warm Shelter, and Grounded Refuge grant 12% increased attack speed (from 20%).

#### Tornado

- Charged Storm casts Storm Bolt at an enemy within 5 meters (from 8).
- Overcast Skies grants 20% increased Storm Bolt targeting range (from 35%). Max 3 points (from 4).

- Unending Storm now also removes Rampage's traversal tag.

##### Shaman

- Eternal Storm grants 7% increased minion elemental damage per point (from minion cold and lightning damage).

- Updated the buff icons for Aspect of the Boar, Aspect of the Shark, Aspect of the Lynx, and Aspect of the Viper.

### Mage

#### Arcane Ascendance

- Superconductor now displays a tooltip for Static.

#### Black Hole

- Endless Maw now adds 2 seconds to the cooldown duration per point (from 15% less cooldown recovery speed per point, insufficiently described as just "cooldown recovery speed"). This is a buff.

#### Disintegrate

- Charge Conduit now displays a tooltip for Lightning Blast instead of Static.

#### Elemental Nova

- Arcane Protection's description has been corrected to state "additional ward retention" (previously said more ward retention).
- Immolation has a max of 4 points (from 8).
- Infernal Nova requires 2 points in Immolation (from 4).
- Glacial Might grants 22% more damage per point (from 18%). Max 4 points (from 5).
- Protective Strikes has been replaced with Elemental Expulsion: Direct casts have a 4% chance per point to repeat a short distance away from you. This chance is multiplied by the number of types of Elemental Nova you have enabled. These repeats can hit the same enemies again. Max 3 points.
- Magical Barrier has been replaced with Ire of the Elements: Recasts from Elemental Expulsion will instead target random enemies within 12 meters. +2 mana cost. Max 1 point.
- Spark Charges grants +25% spark charge chance per point (from 20%). Max 4 points (from 5).
- Overcharge grants 12% chance per point to be overcharged (from 8%). Max 4 points (from 5).

#### Fire Ball

- Flamethrower no longer prevents mana regeneration while channeling. Its description now has reminder text stating that channeled skills have a minimum mana cost of 1.

#### Mana Strike

- Breaking Current's description now states it grants a chance to shred armor (previously incorrectly said shred physical resistance).

#### Static Orb

- Arcane Current's alt text has been clarified to state it does not apply to the explosion or its tendrils.

#### Firebrand

- Now has 150% damage effectiveness (from 125%).
- Incineration grants 15% more damage (from 12%) per stack of Firebrand for your next melee attack other than Firebrand.
- Illuminating Fire grants +4% critical strike multiplier (from 2%) per stack of Firebrand per point when consuming stacks of Firebrand.

- Chains now prioritize enemies over destructible objects.

#### Runic Invocation

- Adjusted the description of Stride to Safety to clarify it grants more damage for direct casts of Runic Invocation.
- We've performed a pass on invocations in order to improve those that were underperforming. In all cases where an invocation's damage effectiveness was increased, its base damage has also been increased by an equivalent amount. For example, if an invocation went from 150% to 250% effectiveness, its base damage was also raised from 30 to 50.
- Twin Embers (Rah): Now has 250% effectiveness (from 150%).
- Rune Shard (Heo): Now has 300% effectiveness (from 200%).
- Crackling Glyph (Gon): Now has 350% effectiveness (from 250% stated, 300% actual).
- Unvar's Eruption (Rah Rah): Now has 350% effectiveness (from 200%).

- Dancing Sparks (Rah Gon): Now has 28 mana cost (from 36) and 300% effectiveness (from 200%).
- Unvar's Eternal Embers (Heo Rah): Now has 20 mana cost (from 24) and 200% effectiveness (from 150% stated, 100% actual).
- Unvar's Ice Glyph (Heo Heo): Now has 30 mana cost (from 37) and 400% effectiveness (from 250%).
- Unvar's Shockwave (Heo Gon): Now has 22 mana cost (from 28) and 300% effectiveness (from 250%).
- Plasma Blast (Gon Rah): Now has 22 mana cost (from 33).
- Unvar's Shatter Bolt (Gon Heo): Now has 30 mana cost (from 36) and 300% effectiveness (from 200%). Its max ricochet range is now 12 (from 10), and it can ricochet 6 times (from 5).
- Sea of Sparks (Gon Gon): Now has 30 mana cost (from 36) and 300% effectiveness (from 200%).
- Aergon's Greater Fireball (Rah Rah Rah): Now has 400% effectiveness for the initial hit (from 150%) and 900% effectiveness for the explosion (from 300%).
- Rime Spiral (Rah Rah Heo): Now has 300% effectiveness (from 200%), and now creates 21 projectiles (from 13).
- Echoes of Thunder (Rah Rah Gon): Now has 42 mana cost (from 46) and 400% effectiveness (from 250%).

- Antipode of Mesembria (Rah Gon Heo): Now has 1,500% effectiveness (from 900%).
- Il'kir's Storm Star (Rah Gon Gon): Now creates 8 sparks (from 6), each spark lasts for 4 seconds (from 2.5), and multiple sparks can now damage the same enemy simultaneously.
- Igneous Rain (Heo Rah Rah): Now hits 21 times over its duration (from 12).

##
Item Updates

### Affixes

- The "ward per second and ward decay threshold" affix on rings and amulets grants 2-3 ward per second at tier 1 (from 6-7), 4-5 ward per second at tier 2 (from 8-9), 6-9 ward per second at tier 3 (from 10-11), and 10-14 ward per second at tier 4 (from 12-14).
- The Duskblade's affix on 4x1 Rogue idols grants 2-4% increased Umbral Blades damage per stack of Dusk Shroud (from 4-8%), up to a maximum of 20 stacks (previously did not state the maximum, but was always applied).
- The increased mana "Azure" affix can no longer roll on Sentinel specific items. Instead, the Sentinel has a new hybrid increased mana and mana regen affix, which gives slightly less increased mana than an increased mana affix, and slightly less mana regen than an increased mana regen affix.

### Uniques

- Truesight Glass grants up to 50% chance to deal Deadly Strikes (from up to 40%) based on your critical strike chance above 100%, and now also grants +1 to all skills.
- Carrion of Creation now also grants 12-18% increased attack and cast speed, and the Primordial Blood ability has a base of 50 damage (from 30) and 250% damage effectiveness (from 150%).
- Tabi of Dusk and Dawn's behavior has been adjusted, and now matches the description provided in its alt text: the shadow of the unequipped weapon type is consumed immediately after it attacks (previously that shadow would not be consumed, and was available to be used).
- Sierpin's Factral Tree grants +6-18 dexterity (from 3-12).
- Merophage grants +1-2 to all skills (from 1).
- Celestial Doom's Doom Pulse triggers have a 1 second cooldown each (from 2).
- Trinity of Flames grants 12-24% increased fire spell damage (from 12-16%) and 12-24% chance to ignite on hit (from 12-16), and it no longer grants 36% less critical strike multiplier to the guaranteed critical strike on every third fire spell.
- Taste of Blood grants 20-30% increased bleed duration (from 15%). Its effective level for Legendary Potential is now 30 (from 40).
- Hakar's Phoenix's cooldown on reviving your down companion is now 6 seconds (from 10).
- Undisputed grants +33-55 melee physical damage (from 27-41), and 8% increased physical damage per recent melee hit against a bleeding enemy (from 5%), up to 400% (from 255%). It now also grants +1-2 to level of physical melee skills. It has also received alt text clarifying that dual wielding this weapon causes the effect to build twice as fast, but does not affect the maximum benefit.
- Orb Weaver's Fang now doubles the stats on this item for 5 seconds (from 3) after hitting a boss or rare enemy that is at low health.
- Leviathan Carver grants +80-120 physical melee damage (from 60-90), and +10-20% physical penetration (from 6-12%).
- Torkrefin's Hunger grants +2% physical penetration (from 1%) and +20% bleed chance (from 15%) per 5% uncapped physical resistance for attacks that expend a stack of Viscera.
- Torkrefin's Hunger grants a 20% chance to grant a stack of Viscera on kill or when hitting a boss or rare enemy (previously only on kill).
- Volcanus now fires its Magma Shards in a forwards cone, targeting enemies within that cone. Magma Shards can now hit the same enemy multiple times from a single cast, but it fires 4 projectiles per cast (from 5).
- Bloodkeeper's Nest grants 8% of minion physical damage leeched as health (from 4%), and when you directly cast Thorn Shield, the two nearest Bees also gain Thorn Shield (from only the nearest Bee).
- Murama's Hilt grants +1-2 to curse skills.
- Ribbons of Blood grants +1-2 to minion skills.
- Hollow Finger grants +1-2 to Summon Skeleton.
- Scavenger grants 40-200% increased chance to find potions (from 40-120%), and now also grants +1-2 potion slots.
- Fighting Chance grants 6-12% increased damage taken (from 5-10%), 6-12% increased movement speed (from 5-10%), and now also grants 6-12% increased melee attack speed.
- Alluvion's Tidal Wave can now also be triggered by indirect melee attacks, matching its description.
- Death's Embrace's description has been updated to clarify you gain a stack of Harrowing Claim when you directly use Harvest and hit at least one enemy (previously did not say directly). This is only a description change.
- Event Horizon's description has been updated to clarify you gain Dilation when you directly use a melee attack and hit at least one enemy (previously did not say directly). This is only a description change.
- Jasper's Searing Pride's description has been updated to clarify you gain Searing Blades when you directly use a melee attack and hit at least one enemy (previously did not say directly). This is only a description change.
- Scales of Eterra's description has been updated to clarify you gain an Infusion when directly casting a cold/fire/lightning spell (previously did not say directly). This is only a description change.
- Serpent's Milk no longer has "minions deal 90% less poison damage". It now grants +50-100% chance to poison on minion hit (from 200%).
- Wraithlord's Harbour: the Wraithlord's Stygian Beams can now target up to 5 enemies with each cast (from 3).
- Unique idols now inherently include the restriction of limiting you to equipping a maximum of 1 of each unique idol (including Legendary idols).
- Singularity now grants 12-30% more hit damage (from "8-20% more damage if you have only one Singularity equipped").
- The Land Before now grants +4 maximum companions (from "+4 maximum companions if this is your only equipped unique idol").
- Harbinger of Stars: the mana gain on potion use for each Meteor you have cast recently now has a maximum of 200 mana gained from each potion use.
- Fangs of the Berserker grants 10-20% of health leech also drains the health of the nearest enemy within 6 meters while you have frenzy (from 21-35%).
- Rule of the Simoon now also grants +1 to attunement skills.
- Unique items will no longer display roll ranges for modifiers which do not have roll ranges.
- The "less damage over time taken while you have haste" effect found on Advent of the Erased and on the newly added Gift of the Eidolon is capped at granting a maximum of 75% less damage over time taken, after taking increased effect of haste into account.
- Omen of Thunder now grants "When you directly summon a Storm Totem all existing totems gain 24-34 spell lightning damage for 20 seconds" (previously said it does not expire, but had a 60 second duration).

### General

- Updated Early Game Acolyte Body Armor.
- Outcast Rags has new art and grants 13 armor (from 17).
- Heretic Garb grants 19 armor (from 23).
- Added a new early game Acolyte Body Armor subtype, Urix Garb, which requires level 9, and grants 37 armor and 9-13% poison resistance.
- Ribbed Cuirass requires level 17 (from 12).

- Updated Early Game Acolyte Helmets.
- Outcast cage has new art and has been renamed to Pariah Shroud.
- Added a new early game Acolyte Helmet subtype, Spiked Cage, which requires level 11, and grants 15 armor and 3-9 damage reflected to attackers.
- Death Mask requires level 16 (from 13).

- Updated Early Game Rogue Body Armors.
- Cloth Armor now grants 30 armor (from 24).
- Leather Hauberk now also grants +2 health regen.
- Rogues now start with a Roughspun Tunic (from Cloth Armor); this gives 24 armor, like Cloth Armor used to.

- Updated Early Game Rogue Helmets.
- Added a new early game Rogue Helmet subtype, Torn Hood, which has no level requirement and grants 7 armor.
- Cloth Hood now requires level 5 (from no level requirement).
- Bandit Helm now requires level 7 (from 5).
- Visual item changes.

- Updated 3D item art for some glove subtypes for Acolyte and Rogue.
- Updated Worn Boots 2D art.

### Idols

- Idol altars drop with far fewer affixes before 150 Corruption. Below level 50 they have no affixes.

### Items

- Made changes to item corruption rules aimed at reducing the power of corrupted items early in the game. They should still be powerful drops, but less prone to trivialize content by including affixes much too powerful for that point in the game.
- Below area level 80, precorrupted items cannot roll T7 affixes.
- Below area level 50, precorrupted items cannot roll T6 affixes.

- Runes of Corruption used on normal, magic, rare, and exalted items with a level requirement below 55 cannot roll T7 affixes.
- Runes of Corruption used on normal, magic, rare, and exalted items with a level requirement below 35 cannot roll T6 affixes.
- The following corrupted affixes now have a level requirement below which they cannot show up on precorrupted items. This does not affect the Rune of Corruption and does not affect the level required to equip items with these affixes:
- All attributes with at least 7 corrupted non-idol items equipped -> level 40.
- Added Health Regen and Increased Health Regen per Strength -> level 30.
- Added Bow Damage and Increased Bow Attack Speed on Bow Attack -> level 45.
- Added Spell Damage and Increased Spell Damage per Increased Movement Speed -> level 36.
- Increased Cast Speed and Ward gain on direct Spell Cast -> level 36.
- Added Throwing Damage and Throwing Armor Shred Chance -> level 42.
- Mana gained on Potion Use and Ward Gained on Potion Use -> level 48.
- Increased Cast Speed and Ward gain on direct Spell Cast (gloves edition) -> level 43.
- Increased Armor and Damage Reflected to Attackers per Armor Mitigation -> level 45.
- Increased Health and Ward Per Second -> level 50.
- Added Intelligence and Ward Per Second -> level 43.

- Reduced the maximum forging potential cost of Rune of Evolution from 25 to 15.

### Faction Updates

- Item tooltips now show the faction requirement in red if you don't have a high enough rank to use them.
- Added a UI notification when you rank up in any faction.

### The Woven

- If you have the Memories of the Observer Weaver Tree node, resetting an Echo Web with the Sanctuary of Eterra will prevent the Echo Chains at the start of the web spawning with Woven Echoes to their sides.
- Imprinted items drop from enemies and Echo rewards around 20% more often.
- Imprinted items drop from Lost Caches around 40% more often.
- Items dropped by imprint slots are much more likely to keep the high tier affixes of the imprinted item.
- Added three new Weaver Tree nodes relating to the Rage of Morditas mechanic.
- Ubiquity of Rage: Your Echoes are more likely to contain Rage of Morditas encounters.
- Seekers of Ice and Blood: Unique items and item subtypes that are specific to the Rage of Morditas encounter are significantly more common, but Enemies in the second phase of Rage of Morditas encounters deal more damage.
- Portents of Blood: A single random enemy in the second phase of Rage of Morditas encounters is replaced by a random Omen, and a pile of corrupted items drops at the end of the encounter.

##
Quality of Life

- Moved the Full Offline mode to be accessible via the landing page after launching the game normally instead of needing to use a Steam launch option.

### UI

- Improved item sorting (stash, inventory) to avoid leaving a single empty column when possible.
- This should make it so you can still quick move or loot items with a width of 2 after sorting a mostly full stash or inventory.

- Display a lowered opacity two-handed icon of the item you are using on the offhand slot to show that it's taking up both slots.
- Updated visuals for in game notifications.
- New Gameplay UI Setting → Side Panels Offset. This allows wide-screen resolution clients the ability to move the left and right UI side panels (Stash, Character, Forge (Left), Inventory, Social (Right)) in and out by a set of resolution dependent intervals. Setting will only appear in extended or ultra wide resolutions (Gameplay → Interface → under Overlay Map Opacity setting).
- Moved Echo reward progress tracker above quests and updated it to not hide when minimizing the quest log, since it is not a quest and is only relevant or shown during the content you are actively completing.

### Stash Adjustments

- Added new Stash search macros:
- skill matches the number of levels granted by any individual level of skill affix.
- e.g. skill4 would match if the item had a T7 (+4) level of skill affix.

- skills matches the total number of levels granted by all level of skill affixes.
- e.g. skills7 would match if the item had a T7 (+4) level of skill affix and a T6 (+3) level of skill affix.

- aff/regex/ or affix/regex/ matches the tier of any affix which had a name that matches the regex.
- e.g. aff/Hybrid Health/7 would match if the item had a T7 Hybrid Health affix.

- Updated UI key glyphs.

### Controller

- Improvements to the Item Faction user interfaces with controllers.
- The virtual cursor has been removed. All interfaces should now be natively interactable using standard controller buttons or thumbsticks.

### Performance

- Optimized the performance of how assets are loaded into scenes.
- Introduced a system for reducing VFX complexity when multiple instances of abilities are spawned, which improves performance in heated battles.
